newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria, Russia to speed up gas pipeline project.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria, Russia to speed up gas pipeline project.

text.p: Bulgaria and Russia plan to speed up a long-delayed pipeline project for transporting Russian natural gas to the Balkans through Bulgaria, officials said on Tuesday.

Russia's Deputy Prime Minister Oleg Lobov and his Bulgarian counterpart Alexander Bozhkov signed a protocol on energy, trade and other issues, preparing the agenda of an intergovernmental committee meeting planned for June.

"The two sides are interested in supplying natural gas to Bulgaria and transiting it through Bulgarian territory and construction work will be started under a contract between Topenergy and Bulgargas," Bozhkov told a news conference after signing the protocol.
He added the Bulgarian government should guarantee the return of Topenergy's investments, while Gazprom should guarantee natural gas supplies.
"In this respect the necessary measures will be taken so that Topenergy will be able to import construction materials duty free," Bozhkov said.

Bulgaria's interim Prime Minister Stefan Sofianski confirmed on Monday that Bulgaria would cancel two pipeline concessions for transiting Russian gas announced by the previous government as they violate the concession law.
Bulgarian and Russian experts would prepare an alternative scheme within two weeks to enable construction work to start in a very short time, Bozhkov said.

Gazprom holds 50 percent in the joint stock company Topenergy, which was set up in Bulgaria in 1995 together with Bulgaria's Bulgargas, which has 25.1 percent. The remaining 24.9 percent are distributed among Bulgarian banks and firms.

Last year Topenergy asked for a concession for transiting pipelines. An enlargement of the network will be needed because gas supplies to Turkey will be increased and the project envisages gas supplies to Greece, Macedonia, Serbia and possibly Albania in the future, officials said.
"Russia needs to invest some $600 million in the gas pipeline system," Lobov told reporters after talks with President Petar Stoyanov on Tuesday.

"The President backed our agreements and in the coming days the necessary documents will be prepared to start the realisation of the (gas) project...We discussed (with him) the development of Bulgaria's gas network," Lobov said.
Bulgaria has a gas network of some 2,000 km, including links to Turkey, Greece and Macedonia, and plans to construct a new link to Serbia.

Bozhkov said an intergovernmental agreement would be prepared within a month for settling Bulgaria's payments for Gazprom annual supplies of 3.4 billion cubic metres through Topenergy in the next 10 years.
Part of the payment will be made in hard currency and the remainder by barter and construction and other services, Bozhkov said.
